cards.title: Introduction to Flask Views
cards.content:
In Flask, Views are the functions that respond to web requests. They handle the business logic and return a response, which is typically rendered HTML, JSON, or plain text.

Flask uses the @app.route() decorator to bind a URL to a specific view function.

from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def home():
    return 'Hello, World!'

cards.title: Return Types in Flask Views
cards.content:
Flask views can return various data types:

  • Strings: Converted into an HTML response by Flask.
  • Dictionaries: Automatically converted into a JSON response (Flask 1.1+).
  • Response Objects: Created using make_response() for custom status codes and headers.
  • Rendered Templates: Using render_template() to serve HTML files.

content.sentence: To render an HTML template named index.html inside a view, you use the function ___('index.html').

cards.title: Handling HTTP Methods
cards.content:
By default, a Flask route only answers to GET requests. You can handle other HTTP methods like POST, PUT, or DELETE by passing the methods argument to the route decorator.

from flask import request

@app.route('/login', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def login():
    if request.method == 'POST':
        return 'Logging in...'
    return 'Render login form'

cards.title: Match HTTP Methods to Use Cases
Variable Rules in Routes
cards.content:
You can add variable sections to a URL by marking sections as <variable_name>. Your view function then receives the value as a keyword argument.

@app.route('/user/<username>')
def profile(username):
    return f'User profile for {username}'

You can also specify converters like <int:user_id> or <float:price>.

steps: Client sends an HTTP request to the server.
Flask matches the URL path to a registered route.
The corresponding view function executes and processes logic.
The view returns a response object or rendered template.
Flask sends the HTTP response back to the client.

cards.title: Conclusion
cards.content:
You have learned how to create basic views, handle multiple HTTP methods, return various data types, utilize URL variables, and structure the request lifecycle in Flask.
